pk.context: 30 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: opaque, pink and black delayed-release capsule

tell: A benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor whose granules are enteric-coated because the drug is acid-labile.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is over 80%. Taken 30 minutes after food, peak levels and exposure fall by about 50% to 70%, and the drug is 97% bound to plasma proteins.
The active moiety has a molecular weight of 369.4. It is a crystalline powder that melts with decomposition at approximately 166°C.
Approved under an NDA as 30 mg delayed-release capsules, with orally disintegrating tablets at 15 and 30 mg.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to any component and with rilpivirine-containing products; abdominal pain and diarrhea are the common reactions.
Active duodenal and benign gastric ulcers, NSAID-associated gastric ulcer, H. pylori eradication, GERD, erosive esophagitis, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

Specifically inhibits the (H+, K+)-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell, blocking the final step of acid production. It lacks anticholinergic or histamine type-2 antagonist activity.
The generic name begins with L and has twelve letters.
